stories.title: Australian MP Helen Haines critically injured after being struck by a car in Wangaratta
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a car outside her Wangaratta constituency office on Monday afternoon and was taken to a Melbourne hospital where she remains in critical condition. Police detained a 43‑year‑old man from nearby Tarrawingee after a passerby stopped the vehicle, and a knife was found inside the car. Investigators are assessing whether the collision was intentional, but have said there is no ongoing community threat.
stories.why: The incident underscores the vulnerability of elected officials to violence and the need for effective security measures.

stories.title: US stocks rebound as AI and chip shares recover ahead of earnings
stories.summary: On 19 Oct 2026 US equity indexes rose, with the Nasdaq 100 up about 1.2% and the S&P 500 gaining roughly 0.6% after a sharp sell‑off the day before. Semiconductor and AI‑linked stocks led the rally; CoreWeave jumped 3% after a Goldman Sachs upgrade and SpaceX and Tesla advanced ahead of their earnings releases. The move came as investors returned to technology names ahead of a busy earnings week.
stories.why: The rally occurred ahead of a busy earnings week, potentially shaping expectations for upcoming tech reports.

stories.title: Trump waives Russia sanctions, easing India’s energy concerns as US trade deal nears
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump waived key Russian sanctions which may enhance trade relations with India. This decision is expected to provide negotiating space for a potential trade deal.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: US very close to finalising trade deal with India, says Marco Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Monday that Washington is close to finalising a trade deal with India. He noted that energy supply considerations are among the factors taken into account when deciding on national security waivers related to Russian oil and gas sanctions.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.

stories.title: Anthropic creates public‑benefit fund funded by 5% of its shares
stories.summary: Anthropic announced it is establishing a wholly‑owned public‑benefit fund and will allocate 5% of its shares to it. The fund can receive an additional 2% of shares for each 50% increase in Anthropic’s valuation and may make large donations to nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations. The company also reaffirmed a $200 million commitment to study AI’s impact on employment.
stories.why: The fund provides a mechanism for Anthropic to allocate resources toward societal‑good projects.
stories.previousTitle: Anthropic to allocate 5% of its shares to public‑benefit fund
stories.previousSummary: Anthropic announced it will set aside 5 % of its outstanding shares in a wholly‑owned public‑benefit fund. The fund can make large donations to nonprofit organisations and direct distributions to address societal challenges such as AI’s impact on employment, and it will not be used for lobbying or political contributions. The company also said it may increase the fund’s stake by an additional 2 % for every 50 % rise in Anthropic’s valuation.
